prompt:
Creating a planet called Frost Nova for a Roblox exploration game sounds like a fantastic project! Since your theme is "ruins and relics," you can lean into a "Frozen Civilization" aesthetic.

Here is a breakdown of how to design and build Frost Nova:

1. The Visual Concept (The "Nova" look)

The name "Frost Nova" suggests something more intense than just a regular ice planet. Think of it as a planet that was once a sun or a tropical paradise that was instantly flash-frozen.

Color Palette: Deep navy blues, piercing cyan, and glowing white. Use neon parts sparingly to represent "Frozen Energy."
Terrain: Instead of just flat snow, use the Roblox Terrain Editor to create jagged "Ice Spikes" (Glacial formations) and deep ravines. Use the Ice and Snow materials, but mix in Basalt for the dark, rocky ground beneath the ice.
Atmosphere: Go to Lighting > Atmosphere . Set the Density higher to create a foggy blizzard effect, and set the Color to a light blue to make the air feel cold.

2. The Ruins (Where the relics are)

Since the game is about ruins, you want the structures to look like they were swallowed by the frost.

The "Shattered Observatory": A massive dome made of "SmoothPlastic" (simulating ancient stone) that has been cracked open by giant ice crystals growing through it.
Frozen Hallways: Use "Glass" material with high transparency and a blue tint to create walls of ice that have ancient carvings visible inside them.
Mechanic Idea: Maybe players have to use a "Heat Lantern" tool to melt thin ice barriers to enter the ruins.

3. The Relics (The loot)

To fit the "Frost Nova" theme, the relics should feel cold or energetic.

The Glacial Heart: A pulsing blue crystal that hums.
Nova Shards: Fragments of the planet's original core, which could be used to upgrade the player's cold-resistance gear.
Cryo-Scrolls: Ancient documents frozen in blocks of ice that tell the story of how the planet became Frost Nova.

4. Roblox Technical Tips

Particle Effects: Create a ParticleEmitter in a large transparent part over the whole map. Use a small white circle texture with a bit of "Transparency" and "Speed" to create a falling snow effect.
Environment Sounds: Search the Roblox Creator Store for "Wind Howl" or "Ice Cracking" sounds. Set them to Looped = true to build the atmosphere.
Lighting Effects: Add a ColorCorrectionEffect in Lighting and slightly increase the Saturation and Contrast to make the blue crystals really pop against the white snow.

Would you like me to help you generate a "Brief" for this project, or perhaps create some concept art for what a "Frost Nova Ruin" might look like?
enriched: Create a 3D game map depicting the frozen planet Frost Nova, an intense icy world with a deep navy blue and cyan color palette accented by glowing white and subtle neon elements representing frozen energy. The terrain features jagged ice spikes and deep ravines formed from glacial formations, blending ice and snow materials with dark basalt rock beneath. The atmosphere is thick with a light blue foggy blizzard effect, enhancing the cold, harsh environment. In the midground, place the ruins of a shattered observatory-a massive cracked dome made of smooth plastic simulating ancient stone, pierced by giant ice crystals. Surrounding the observatory are frozen hallways with translucent blue-tinted glass walls etched with ancient carvings, partially encased in ice. Scattered throughout the ruins are relics such as pulsing blue crystals called Glacial Hearts, glowing Nova Shards embedded in the ground, and blocks of ice containing Cryo-Scrolls. The scene includes subtle particle effects of falling snow and ambient sounds of wind and ice cracking to immerse players in the frozen, mysterious environment.

prompt:
Game Name (working title)
LAST ROUTE
"No one knows why the road is still open."
Core Idea
You and up to 5 friends are driving one truck across a frozen mountain to deliver the last generator core to a dying town.
Without it...
Thousands of people freeze.
So turning back isn't an option.
Core Gameplay Loop
Drive ⬇ Reach checkpoint ⬇ Random event ⬇ Solve it together ⬇ Repair truck ⬇ Continue ⬇ Repeat ⬇ Final escape
The truck almost never stops for long. The journey is the game.
The BIG Hook
The Storm Changes Every Run.
Not just weather.
The storm changes the world.
Examples:
🌨 Heavy snow.
Visibility 5 metres.
🧊 Frozen lake.
Road disappears.
Drive over ice.
Risk breaking through.
🌲 Fallen trees.
Need axes.
⛰ Avalanche.
New road opens.
Old road closes.
📡 Strange radio signal.
Follow it...
Or ignore it.
🏚 Abandoned village appears.
Sometimes.
Not every run.
Every run feels different.
Player Jobs
Everyone naturally gets a role.
🚛 Driver
Can only focus on driving.
🗺 Navigator
Uses map.
Finds routes.
Reads signs.
🔧 Mechanic
Repairs truck.
Keeps engine alive.
Changes tyres.
📦 Scavenger
Searches buildings.
Gets fuel.
Food.
Medicine.
Parts.
🔦 Lookout
Uses binoculars.
Warns about danger.
Nobody is standing around.
The Horror
No zombie waves.
No screaming monster.
Something...
Is following the truck.
It never attacks directly.
Instead...
Fuel disappears.
Doors open.
Lights go out.
Tyre tracks appear beside yours.
Someone knocks...
But nobody is there.
The mystery is the horror.
Mid Game Twist
You discover...
Every abandoned truck looks exactly like yours.
Same number.
Same cargo.
Same scratches.
How?
Nobody knows.
Now players start theorising.
Final Act
The storm gets insane.
Truck barely works.
Visibility almost zero.
Radio cuts in.
Someone says...
"Don't let it overtake you."
Now everyone panics.
You don't even know what "it" is.
Ending
Reach the town.
Unload generator.
Lights come on.
Storm instantly stops.
Outside...
Your truck has six sets of footprints around it.
Nobody says anything.
Game ends.
Players immediately start discussing what happened.
Why I think this is stronger
The mystery is what people remember.
Not:
"Big monster killed me."
But:
"WHY WAS THERE ANOTHER TRUCK?"
Those kinds of mysteries create YouTube theory videos.
MVP (cheap version)
One truck.
One mountain road.
Three checkpoints.
10-15 random events.
One ending.
No giant open world.
No massive AI.
The game could be finished in about 20-30 minutes per run.
But here's the one thing I'd still change.
I wouldn't make it a pure horror game.
I'd make it 70% adventure, 30% horror.
If players are scared the whole time, the fear wears off. If most of the game is about teamwork, driving, and making decisions, then the strange moments hit much harder because they're unexpected.
One last thing: if your goal is a viral Roblox game, don't try to beat Dead Rails by adding more monsters or more mechanics. Beat it by making players ask one question after every run:
"Wait... what actually happened out there?"
That kind of mystery gives people a reason to replay, tell their friends, and watch theory videos. That's much harder to copy than just another survival game.

4. UI Tracker: A clean ScreenGui tracking the player's current stage and showing a timer.
